title: Tiny satellite will use the dark side of the Moon as a shield
summary: Researchers at Cambridge University are developing a small satellite mission that will position itself behind the Moon to use its far side as a natural radio shield, blocking Earth's interfering signals to detect extremely faint 21cm hydrogen signals from the cosmic dark ages—the early universe approximately 13 billion years ago.
problem_solved: Overcoming Earth's pervasive radio frequency interference (RFI) that drowns out the extremely faint 21cm hydrogen line signals from the early universe, which are impossible to detect from our planet.
why_valuable: It could provide humanity's first direct observation of the 'cosmic dark ages' and the birth of the first stars and galaxies—information that is otherwise lost and unobservable from Earth.
